title: EVERY CHANGE SHOULD BE REVERSIBLE
script:
Giving an AI write access without version history is like letting someone renovate your house with no before photos.

Every change should leave a trail.

Save a checkpoint before the work starts.

Show exactly what changed.

Let the agent test the result.

And if the new version is worse, roll back instead of patching over the mistake.

Good automation doesn’t just move fast.

It makes every step reversible.
audience: People using AI coding agents, automation tools and assistants.
concept: The Reversible Rowhouse Folio uses one persistent paper house and an exposed paper-gold mechanical archive. Bot begins an unsafe roof overwrite, but the falling original roof physically trips a spring catch that preserves both roof states. Bot then engages a pressure-cam checkpoint, installs the visibly different coral roof through the same connected drive, performs a physical rain test, and observes a real wet, sagging floor. A two-handed rollback archives the actual coral roof and actual wet floor together while restoring the checkpointed dry floor and original roof. The repeated test passes, and a visibly driven reduced three-state display folds back to the exact opening HOUSE identity.
rationale: The revision keeps the rowhouse metaphor while removing unexplained automation, overloaded comparison choreography, compound selectors and the false reappearance of failed evidence. Each autonomous movement now follows a visible latch, spring, rack, cam or Bot-operated control. Every consequential contact has an exact local frame, actor, target, finite state change and affine rule. The finale shows only two reduced archive bays beside the live house: the checkpoint profile and one failed bay containing the actual coral roof and actual wet floor. This leaves the opening and final roof, windows and dry floor readable at native 360×640.

shots.narration: Giving an AI write access without version history is like letting someone renovate your house with no before photos.
physical_sequence: Establish the intact cream rowhouse with its offset teal roof, three uneven windows and level cream floor.
Bot turns the charcoal write latch; its exposed linkage opens the discard mouth and advances the coral roof on a visible rack.
Bot lifts the teal roof from both keyed slots, releases it above the discard path, then recognizes the danger.
Bot presses the latch’s separate brake face; the connected rack stops the coral roof short of the empty slots while the released teal roof continues toward the registered trip latch.
shots.consequence: The opening configuration is visibly endangered, but the proposed roof is mechanically stopped before it can overwrite the empty anchors.

quality.purpose: Make unversioned write access physically dangerous and establish the exact HOUSE state that must return.
quality.hero: The intact rowhouse becoming an unresolved two-roof overwrite.
quality.primary_action: Bot activates the linked write mechanism, removes the original roof and brakes the advancing replacement too late to prevent the original from falling.
quality.before: The teal roof occupies both slots; the windows and cream floor are unchanged and dry.
quality.after: The roof slots are empty, the coral roof is braked short of them and the released teal roof is descending toward the archive trip latch.
secondary_motion: Bot’s antenna turns from the advancing coral roof to the falling teal roof.
The released teal eave flexes for four frames after leaving Bot’s hand.
The exposed write rack compresses against its brake stop without moving unrelated house parts.
environment: Warm-cream tabletop with a deckled front edge
Charcoal pinboard seam behind the roofline
Paper-gold archive rail fixed to the house’s left side
quality.exit_overlap: The teal eave reaches the registered discard-trip-latch as the shot ends.

energy.dominant_action: The original roof is removed and released while the linked replacement drive is abruptly braked.
energy.character_response: Bot changes from focused leverage to a wide surprised brake press.
energy.local_reaction: Only the released roof, braked coral roof and supported façade respond.
energy.residual_motion: The teal eave and Bot antenna retain brief paper lag.
energy.next_action_overlap: The falling eave is already entering the trip latch’s six-frame pre-impact window.

events.state_change: Opening HOUSE state is visible: teal roof seated, three windows exposed, cream floor level and dry.
events.affine_rule: Hold every house part at its registered opening transform.

events.state_change: Right hand seats on write-latch.grip; discard mouth and coral drive are mechanically armed.
events.affine_rule: Solve the canonical right-hand inverse grip to write-latch.grip after the latch reaction transform.

events.state_change: The turned latch releases the write-drive rack; discard mouth opens and coral roof begins advancing.
events.affine_rule: Freeze the latch at its turned stop, release the hand constraint, then translate the connected rack and coral-replacement-roof along their bounded rail.

events.state_change: Right hand seats on teal-original-roof.eave and begins lifting the roof from both slots.
events.affine_rule: Apply the roof lift transform, then solve the right-hand inverse grip to teal-original-roof.eave.

events.state_change: The teal roof leaves the hand constraint and begins a bounded gravity descent toward discard-trip-latch.trip.
events.affine_rule: Preserve the roof’s release pose and continue with the finite descent transform; remove the inverse-grip constraint at this frame.

events.state_change: The falling eave enters the trip latch approach path while retaining its persistent roof identity.
events.affine_rule: Map teal-original-roof.eave to the registered trip path without changing scale or part ownership.

events.state_change: Left hand presses write-latch.brake-grip and engages the rack brake.
events.affine_rule: Resolve the authored left arm to write-latch.brake-grip after Bot performance and latch reaction transforms.

events.state_change: The connected rack stops the coral roof twelve authoring pixels before either roof slot.
events.affine_rule: Clamp write-drive-rack and coral-replacement-roof at the declared brake stop; retain two pixels of local compression only.

shots.narration: Every change should leave a trail.
physical_sequence: The falling teal eave strikes the visible discard-trip latch.
The latch releases an exposed paper leaf spring connected to the gold catch tongue and segmented history strip.
The driven tongue hooks the teal eave before the discard mouth; successive owned strip segments unfold and carry the roof into the original-state bay.
The same linkage seats the waiting coral roof in the adjacent proposed-state bay and closes the discard mouth.
shots.consequence: The endangered original and waiting replacement become two physically ordered, connected roof states.

quality.purpose: Turn the released roof itself into the visible cause of a persistent change trail.
quality.hero: The spring-driven paper-gold catch and its two ordered roof bays.
quality.primary_action: The falling roof trips the latch that catches it and unfolds the connected history strip.
quality.before: The teal roof is falling toward an open discard mouth; the coral roof remains on the braked write rack.
quality.after: The teal and coral roofs occupy consecutive owned bays on the unfolded history strip, and the discard mouth is closed.
secondary_motion: History-strip segments open successively from the spring-owned inner segment to the outer bay.
The hooked teal roof overshoots its bay by four pixels and returns.
The discard mouth closes only after both roof bay seats are occupied.

energy.dominant_action: The falling roof trips a visible spring mechanism that catches and records both roof states.
energy.local_reaction: The trip latch, catch tongue and contacted teal roof react in sequence.
energy.residual_motion: The outer owned strip segment settles last.
energy.next_action_overlap: Bot reaches for the retained teal roof before the final fold loses all motion.

events.state_change: Roof motion changes from free descent to spring-driven catch travel.

events.state_change: The spring output begins opening owned history segments from inner to outer.
events.affine_rule: Drive each named segment hinge from its own local pivot; do not transform the whole strip as one articulated part.

events.state_change: The caught teal roof seats in the original-state roof notch.

events.state_change: The connected rack seats the coral roof in the adjacent proposed-state bay.
events.affine_rule: Translate the coral roof along the owned rack rail and align its two keys to the proposed bay sockets.

events.state_change: The spring reaches its finite stop; both bays remain connected and the discard mouth closes.
events.affine_rule: Clamp every segment at its declared hinge angle and close the discard mouth on its separate bounded transform.

shots.narration: Save a checkpoint before the work starts.
physical_sequence: Bot returns the retained teal roof to both façade slots and releases it only after the two keyed landings.
Bot grips the checkpoint tab and pulls the gold plate against registered rear stops behind the intact house.

A visible pressure cam rolls across the plate, mechanically setting roof-profile, window-position and floor-level relief shutters; its stored cream dry-floor cassette is locked as part of the checkpoint.
The plate retracts into the archive slot. Its final seat arms and releases the connected comparison drive for the next shot.
shots.consequence: The untouched roof, window arrangement and dry floor state are mechanically registered before the coral roof is installed.

quality.purpose: Show checkpointing as pressure, registration and storage rather than an unexplained appearing relief.
quality.hero: The intact rowhouse pressed against its full-height gold checkpoint plate.
quality.primary_action: Bot restores the opening house, then pulls a plate through a visible pressure-cam capture and into its archive stop.
quality.before: The teal roof is retained in the history bay, and the checkpoint relief shutters are unset.
quality.after: The live house is intact while the archived plate holds latched roof, window, floor-level and dry-floor-cassette states.
secondary_motion: Bot’s roof hand follows the eave anchor until both keys land.
The cam’s small follower wheels rotate only while pressure crosses registered house features.
The checkpoint tab rebounds once at the archive stop.

energy.local_reaction: The pressure cam, plate and tab react without shaking the live house globally.
energy.residual_motion: The tab and cam follower settle at their mechanical stops.
energy.next_action_overlap: The released comparison spring begins moving its visible rack.

physical_sequence: Continue the exposed comparison spring and rack already released by the checkpoint plate.
The rack withdraws the teal roof into the left checkpoint-profile bay while advancing the coral roof toward the same two live slots.

The rack stops with both profiles sharing one large horizontal baseline, leaving the lost pitch, flat deck and drainage notch readable during a dedicated recognition hold.

shots.narration: Let the agent test the result.
physical_sequence: Bot grips the raised rain-ribbon anchor and pulls the translucent strip at a measured constant speed.
One large teal test-water slug reaches the coral drainage notch, exits the roof edge and strikes the upper window flap.
The slug enters the house and impacts the floor at one unambiguous point.
A clipped teal wet mask spreads across the persistent floor strip, then the same strip bends into its finite asymmetric fourteen-pixel sag while Bot holds for recognition.
shots.consequence: The controlled test physically produces a wet, sagging interior floor that persists into rollback.

quality.purpose: Show one readable water path and a persistent physical failure at mobile size.
quality.hero: The coral-roof rowhouse, one large test-water slug and the deforming floor.
quality.primary_action: Bot pulls the test ribbon; its water slug traverses the roof notch and window before wetting and bending the floor.
quality.before: The coral roof is installed; the ribbon is raised and the floor is cream, level and dry.
quality.after: The test-water slug has entered the house; the actual floor strip is fully wet and held in its asymmetric sag state.
secondary_motion: Bot’s pulling hand remains solved to rain-ribbon-anchor.grip until the end of the pull.
The water slug compresses only at the notch and window contacts.
The floor wet mask and sag stop at declared finite states; no global house shake is added.

energy.local_reaction: Only the coral notch, window flap and actual floor strip answer the water path.
energy.residual_motion: The wet floor fibers settle into their persistent sag.
energy.next_action_overlap: Bot reaches for rollback without touching or patching the failed parts.

shots.narration: And if the new version is worse, roll back instead of patching over the mistake.
physical_sequence: Bot places its left and right hands on the separately named checkpoint-tab grips and begins one braced pull.
The linked carriage removes the coral roof into the failed-state bay; a lower floor shuttle removes the actual wet, sagging floor into the same bay.
The checkpoint’s stored cream dry-floor cassette enters the live floor mounts while the teal original roof travels on its separate rail toward the façade slots.

The original roof and dry cassette land, the linked take-up reel raises the rain ribbon, and the carriage stops with the actual coral roof and actual wet floor still visible together in the failed bay.
shots.consequence: Rollback restores the checkpointed house while conserving the failed roof and the actual wet floor as one physical failed state.

quality.purpose: Demonstrate restoration by exchanging persistent components, not hiding or recreating damage.
quality.hero: The linked rollback carriage, separate roof rails and lower floor shuttle.
quality.primary_action: Bot’s two-handed checkpoint pull archives the failed roof and wet floor together while reinstalling the original roof and checkpointed dry floor.

quality.after: The teal roof and checkpointed dry floor occupy the live house; the coral roof and actual wet floor occupy one failed-state bay; the rain ribbon is raised.
secondary_motion: Bot’s two authored arms remain attached to different tab anchors throughout the pull.
The roof rails and lower floor shuttle remain visually separated.
The seated teal eave and dry cassette each receive a small local compression, while the failed wet floor retains its wet mask and sag.

shots.narration: Good automation doesn’t just move fast.
physical_sequence: Bot grips and pulls the same reset rain-ribbon anchor through the same measured travel.
The same test-water slug reaches the restored teal pitch and travels outward along the overlapping shingle edge.
The slug transfers into the side gutter and lands in the exterior gold catch cup; the checkpointed cream floor remains level and dry.
After a short recognition hold, Bot presses the exposed return-drive lever, releasing the visibly wound finale spring before leaving the frame.
shots.consequence: The restored version passes the same physical test, and Bot visibly initiates the final history display.

The catch cup dips four pixels at landing and returns.
The dry floor stays deliberately still; Bot’s antenna rises in relief before turning toward the return lever.
